summary: `call_ref` and exception `catch` can drop some fuel accounting, leading to exponential fuel amplification
description:
## Impact

When compiling with the Cranelift backend, Wasmtime's fuel accounting around `call_ref` callsites, and also around the catch (exceptional) path for calls within `try_table`s, can drop any accumulated fuel usage within the callee, resetting to the fuel-remaining before the call. This can lead to exponential fuel amplification, that is, a guest that can run for exponential time using linear fuel, effectively avoiding timeouts or regular periodic yields. This is thus a denial-of-service vulnerability in Wasmtime.

The bug requires the use of fuel (`Config::consume_fuel` or `-W fuel=N` in wasmtime-cli), which is off by default. If fuel is enabled the bug affects any configuration using Cranelift, which is the default unless Winch has been configured, and includes users of the Pulley interpreter.

The bug only affects guests that have the `call_ref` or `try_table` opcodes present. The `call_ref` opcode is part of the function-references proposal to WebAssembly, the `try_table` opcode is part of the exception-handling proposal to WebAssembly, and users can also check if they are affected in specific cases by scanning guest bytecode for either opcode. The bug is present in all versions of Wasmtime that support `call_ref`, `try_table` and fuel. `call_ref` and `try_table` have been supported by default since Wasmtime 47.0.0. 

## Patches

Wasmtime 48.0.3 and 49.0.1 have been released with fixes for this issue.

## Workarounds

Wasmtime embedders that only require periodic interruption may consider the use of epoch interruption (`Config::epoch_interruption`) instead. Epoch interruption is not deterministic as fuel is; if deterministic fuel consumption metering is required, the only workaround is an upgrade to a fixed version of Wasmtime.
